hints: Set $\dfrac{2x-3x^2}{(1-3x)^2}=8$ and simplify to a quadratic in $x$.
Solve the quadratic exactly, then substitute both admissible $x$-values into $y=\dfrac{x^2}{1-3x}$.
walkthrough:
Differentiate $y = \dfrac{x^2}{1 - 3x}$ with respect to $x$ using the quotient rule $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\left(\dfrac{u}{v}\right) = \dfrac{u'v - uv'}{v^2}$:
$$u = x^2 \implies u' = 2x$$
$$v = 1 - 3x \implies v' = -3$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{2x(1 - 3x) - x^2(-3)}{(1 - 3x)^2}$$

Set the gradient of the tangent equal to $8$:
$$\dfrac{2x - 3x^2}{(1 - 3x)^2} = 8$$
$$2x - 3x^2 = 8(1 - 6x + 9x^2)$$
$$2x - 3x^2 = 8 - 48x + 72x^2$$

Rearrange all terms to form a standard quadratic equation:
$$75x^2 - 50x + 8 = 0$$

State the exact coordinates of both points:
$$\left(\dfrac{4}{15}, \dfrac{16}{45}\right) \quad \text{and} \quad \left(\dfrac{2}{5}, -\dfrac{4}{5}\right)$$
